newsitem.title: USA: Cold, dry weather should aid US corn, soy harvests.
newsitem.headline: Cold, dry weather should aid US corn, soy harvests.

text.p: Weather in the U.S. Midwest looks set to remain cold and mostly dry for the next few days, favoring harvesting of corn and soybeans, meteorologists said.

"Harvest weather is great. Very cold temperatures will firm up the ground and the tractors should have no problems getting in and harvesting," Joel Burgio, agricultural meteorologist with Weather Services Corp said.

He noted temperatures in the U.S. Midwest looked set to average 10 to 15 degrees below normal Tuesday through Thursday with highs ranging from the upper 20-degrees Fahrenheit to mid-30s F across the region.
Burgio said there was a chance of light snow in the far west and far south of the U.S. Corn Belt on Wednesday but most of the region should be dry.
More dry weather was forecast for Thursday although Burgio said there was a chance of light showers in western areas Friday and Saturday and in eastern areas Saturday/Sunday.
"They (showers) should be pretty light although there is a slight risk they could be in the light to moderate category," WSC's Burgio said.
Fred Gesser, chief forecaster for Weather Express, also said weather in key areas was mostly favorable for harvesting.
"We could see 2.0 to 4.0 inches of snow today into tomorrow in Nebraska, northwest Iowa, north Missouri and northeast Kansas but that area is mostly done (harvesting corn and soybeans)," he said.
"The east is going to be dry except northeast portions of Ohio and western Michigan," Gesser said.
He noted that in Cuyahoga County in northeast Ohio, there were reports that up to 30 inches of snow had fallen. Similar amounts of snow were also reported in the upper Michigan Peninsula.
